articles.title: GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing
articles.snippet:
GTCR has jointly led a $200 million investment in Sophos through a second-lien term loan raised in connection with the refinancing of the cybersecurity company's existing $2.45 billion first-lien term loan.
The post GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 17, 2026
GTCR Leads $200 Million Second Lien Term Loan For Sophos Refinancing
GTCR has jointly led a $200 million investment in Sophos through a second-lien term loan raised in connection with the refinancing of the cybersecurity company’s existing $2.45 billion first-lien term loan.
Sophos is a portfolio company of Thoma Bravo and provides cybersecurity software and services to approximately 625,000 customers worldwide, primarily small and medium-sized businesses and mid-market organizations.
The company’s offerings include endpoint and network protection as well as managed detection and response services that combine software with outsourced security expertise to monitor customer technology environments.
Sophos expanded its enterprise cybersecurity business in February 2025 through its acquisition of Secureworks, adding an enterprise-focused managed detection and response operation to its platform.
The financing follows the close of GTCR’s inaugural Capital Solutions Fund, which provides customized minority structured investments to established businesses. Other recent Capital Solutions investments include TELUS Health and Solmetex.
GTCR said its familiarity with the cybersecurity sector and ongoing relationship with Thoma Bravo enabled the firm to move quickly on Sophos’ financing requirements. GTCR manages approximately $45 billion in equity capital and has invested more than $35 billion across over 300 companies since its founding in 1980.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are excited to partner with Thoma Bravo and the Sophos management team. Our ongoing dialogue with Thoma Bravo and familiarity with the sector enabled us to move quickly to address Sophos’ financing needs. This transaction reflects our ability to work alongside existing owners and management to structure bespoke capital solutions.”
Jason Prager, Managing Director At GTCR
“GTCR brought a practical, collaborative approach to Sophos’ refinancing. Their understanding of the sector and ability to respond quickly as the process evolved made them a constructive partner, and we appreciate their support for Sophos.”
Erwin Mock, Managing Director And Head Of Capital Markets At Thoma Bravo

articles.title: DailyPay Completes $200 Million ABS With Citi, Bank Of America And Barclays
articles.snippet:
DailyPay completed a $200 million asset-backed securitization of its On-Demand Pay receivables, bringing total debt financing backed by those receivables to about $1.4 billion. The transaction is DailyPay's second ABS issuance.
The post DailyPay Completes $200 Million ABS With Citi, Bank Of America And Barclays appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
DailyPay Completes $200 Million ABS With Citi, Bank Of America And Barclays
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 10, 2026
DailyPay Completes $200 Million ABS With Citi, Bank Of America And Barclays
DailyPay completed a $200 million asset-backed securitization of its On-Demand Pay receivables, bringing total debt financing backed by those receivables to about $1.4 billion. The transaction is DailyPay’s second ABS issuance.
The company completed its first $200 million securitization in June 2025.
DailyPay said it remains the only On-Demand Pay provider to have accessed the asset-backed securities market.
DailyPay’s platform enables employees to access wages they have already earned before their regular payday.
The company funds those transfers without affecting employers’ cash flow or requiring changes to existing payroll systems.
DailyPay serves more than 2,000 employers and more than 6 million employees.
The latest offering included four classes of notes ranging from Class A through Class D.
Morningstar DBRS assigned ratings ranging from AA (sf) to BB (sf).
Citi served as lead bookrunner and structuring agent.
Bank of America and Barclays served as joint bookrunners, while KeyBanc, Scotiabank, and Wells Fargo acted as co-managers.
Latham & Watkins advised DailyPay, while Mayer Brown advised the bookrunners.
DailyPay’s approximately $1.4 billion of receivables-backed financing also includes a $960 million secured credit facility.
KEY QUOTES:
“The strong performance of our inaugural ABS supported another oversubscribed transaction, demonstrating continued investor demand for an asset class we pioneered, helping reduce our cost of capital and broadening our funding base.”
Deepa Subramanian, CFO of DailyPay

articles.title: MONTICELLOAM Provides $195.7 Million Financing For 7-Property Skilled Nursing Portfolio
articles.snippet:
MONTICELLOAM and its affiliates have provided $195.7 million in bridge, mezzanine, and working capital financing for a seven-property skilled nursing portfolio spanning Virginia and Indiana.
The post MONTICELLOAM Provides $195.7 Million Financing For 7-Property Skilled Nursing Portfolio appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
MONTICELLOAM Provides $195.7 Million Financing For 7-Property Skilled Nursing Portfolio
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 3, 2026
MONTICELLOAM Provides $195.7 Million Financing For 7-Property Skilled Nursing Portfolio
MONTICELLOAM and its affiliates have provided $195.7 million in bridge, mezzanine, and working capital financing for a seven-property skilled nursing portfolio spanning Virginia and Indiana.
The financing was provided to a repeat MONTICELLOAM client.
Of the total, $184.7 million consists of bridge and mezzanine loans that will support the refinancing of three skilled nursing communities in Virginia and the acquisition of four skilled nursing communities in Indiana.
An additional $11 million working capital line of credit will support day-to-day operating expenses across the portfolio.
The seven facilities collectively contain more than 900 skilled nursing beds.
The financing structure gives the sponsor acquisition capital, refinancing proceeds, and working capital through a single broader transaction.
MONTICELLOAM specializes in financing for senior housing and multifamily properties and provides bridge, working capital, and permanent financing solutions across the U.S.
The platform was founded in 2014 by Alan Litt, Thomas Lally and Jonathan Litt.
KEY QUOTES:
“Skilled nursing operators who are expanding their portfolio need a capital partner that can keep pace with their goals and bring genuine depth to every transaction. Our platform was designed to do exactly that, combining lending expertise, structuring flexibility, and a true understanding of the healthcare real estate landscape.”
Joseph Borenstein, Head of the MONTICELLOAM Healthcare Bridge Lending Team
“We approach every transaction with the goal of providing operators with the stability they need to deliver quality care. This financing gives them room to handle today’s challenges while staying ready for what’s ahead.”
Matthew Lark, Head of Healthcare Underwriting at MONTICELLOAM

articles.title: Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund
articles.snippet:
Boston Financial has closed Boston Financial Institutional Tax Credits 63 Limited Partnership, a $191 million multi-investor Low-Income Housing Tax Credit fund that will support the creation or preservation of 1,342 affordable rental homes across 12 states.
The post Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Boston Financial Closes $191 Million Affordable Housing Tax Credit Fund
Boston Financial has closed Boston Financial Institutional Tax Credits 63 Limited Partnership, a $191 million multi-investor Low-Income Housing Tax Credit fund that will support the creation or preservation of 1,342 affordable rental homes across 12 states.
The fund, known as ITC 63, secured commitments from seven institutional investors and will deploy capital alongside 14 affordable housing developers across 16 communities. The investments will support both new construction projects and preservation efforts for existing affordable housing.
Boston Financial said several developments in the fund will serve populations including seniors, veterans, people with physical or mental disabilities, and formerly unhoused individuals and families.
One of the developments is Choice Landing in Crestwood, Kentucky, which is being developed by nonprofit organization Pillar. The project is expected to provide 72 affordable homes designed to serve adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
Boston Financial estimates that projects supported by ITC 63 will create 2,210 jobs, generate approximately $249 million in wages and business income, and contribute nearly $90 million in tax revenue to local communities.
The fund also benefits from the support of Boston Financial’s parent company, ORIX USA. Boston Financial said ORIX USA’s balance sheet provides additional flexibility and execution capabilities for its affordable housing platform.
Boston Financial has operated in the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit market since the program’s creation in 1986. The firm said it has worked with more than 200 investors to preserve or build over 420,000 affordable homes.
Boston Financial currently manages more than $16.8 billion in affordable housing equity. The firm was founded in 1969 and was acquired by ORIX Corporation USA in 2016.
ORIX USA is a diversified investment and asset management firm focused on credit, real estate, private equity, and managed solutions for middle-market borrowers and investors. The company and its subsidiaries manage $38.8 billion in assets and commitments as of September 22, 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“ITC 63 reflects the strength of the relationships we have built with both our investor and developer partners over many years. We are deeply grateful for the trust our investors place in us and for the extraordinary work our developer partners do every day to bring affordable housing to communities across the country. Their commitment, creativity, and perseverance are making a meaningful difference in the lives of thousands of families, and we are honored to work alongside them in addressing our nation’s housing challenges.”
Rob Golden, CEO Of Boston Financial
“The affordable housing industry succeeds because of collaboration. Each investment in ITC 63 represents a shared commitment among investors, developers, public agencies, and community members to expand and preserve affordable housing opportunities. We are thankful for the confidence our partners continue to place in Boston Financial and proud to help connect capital with high-quality developments that will create lasting impact in communities for years to come.”
John Schromm, Senior Managing Director And Co-Head Of Investor Capital At Boston Financial

articles.title: NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital
articles.snippet:
NorthStar Medical Technologies has secured a multi-year growth capital facility of up to $185 million from Hercules Capital to expand production of no-carrier-added Actinium-225 and its radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities. The financing includes $100 million available upfront.
The post NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 5, 2026
NorthStar Secures Up To $185 Million Growth Financing From Hercules Capital
NorthStar Medical Technologies has secured a multi-year growth capital facility of up to $185 million from Hercules Capital to expand production of no-carrier-added Actinium-225 and its radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capabilities. The financing includes $100 million available upfront.
NorthStar plans to use the capital to increase isotope production and expand clinical and commercial drug manufacturing at its vertically integrated radiopharmaceutical campus.
The company operates co-located isotope production capabilities and a Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization providing cGMP services.
NorthStar is developing production capacity around no-carrier-added Actinium-225, an isotope used in targeted alpha therapies for cancer.
In January 2026, NorthStar became the first company to produce commercial-scale no-carrier-added Ac-225 using electron-accelerator technology.
The company also expanded a partnership with Convergent to support late-stage clinical studies and anticipated commercial demand.
More recently, the FDA accepted NorthStar’s Drug Master File for no-carrier-added Ac-225, providing pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies with a regulatory pathway for incorporating the isotope into clinical and commercial radiopharmaceutical programs.
NorthStar plans to transition to a higher-capacity Ac-225 production line later in 2026.
The company currently has supply and manufacturing agreements with more than 30 pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers, including several large developers of Ac-225-based therapies.
KEY QUOTES:
“NorthStar is executing on our vision to become the radiopharmaceutical industry’s most comprehensive strategic supply-chain partner. This commitment from Hercules provides the necessary capital to expand our capacity, accelerate our growth, and support our partners as they advance innovative therapies to patients across the world.”
Dr. Frank Scholz, President and CEO of NorthStar
“NorthStar has demonstrated the ability to produce a critical isotope at scale at an important time for the industry. We are pleased to provide capital to help NorthStar expand its production and meet growing demand, while supporting its role as a partner to companies advancing these therapies.”
Lake McGuire, Managing Director of Hercules Capital

articles.title: Terra Secures $183.75 Million Refinancing From Monroe Capital For The Offices At THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands
articles.snippet:
Terra has secured a $183.75 million loan from Monroe Capital's Real Estate Platform to refinance The Offices at THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands, the recently completed Class A office component of Terra's wellness-focused mixed-use development in South Florida.
The post Terra Secures $183.75 Million Refinancing From Monroe Capital For The Offices At THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Terra Secures $183.75 Million Refinancing From Monroe Capital For The Offices At THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Terra Secures $183.75 Million Refinancing From Monroe Capital For The Offices At THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands
Terra has secured a $183.75 million loan from Monroe Capital’s Real Estate Platform to refinance The Offices at THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands, the recently completed Class A office component of Terra’s wellness-focused mixed-use development in South Florida.
The refinancing follows completion of the 96,000-square-foot office building during the summer of 2026. The property is already more than 90% leased, with tenants including Man Capital, Dwight Capital, TEB Capital Management, NewCo Capital Group, and Legacy Wealth Advisors. The Golden Good Market and THE WELL Club are expected to open on the ground floor in 2027.
The Offices at THE WELL is part of THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands, which Terra describes as the first THE WELL-branded office and residential project in the United States. The broader development includes an eight-story residential component with 65 luxury residences and more than 22,000 square feet of amenities.
Terra designed the property around the integration of workplace, hospitality, and wellness. Office amenities include rooftop meeting and gathering spaces, community gardens, fitness programming, an elevated outdoor courtyard, health coaching, concierge services, and spa privileges. The residential amenity program includes a wellness center and THE WELL Club.
Monroe Capital’s Real Estate Platform provides structured debt and equity financing across property types and markets. The financing expands Monroe’s middle-market real estate activity while providing Terra with long-term capital following the building’s completion and leasing ramp.
Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory represented Terra in the transaction. The advisory team was led by Keith Kurland, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer, and Jordan Casella.
Terra is also developing THE WELL Coconut Grove in Miami and has developed more than eight million square feet of residential, commercial, and mixed-use projects across South Florida.
KEY QUOTES:
“Securing this refinancing following the building’s completion and strong leasing performance speaks to the strength of the project and the demand we’re seeing for a more wellness-focused workplace. We set out to create an office environment that rethinks the relationship between work and wellness, and the response from tenants has validated that vision.”
David Martin, CEO Of Terra
“We are excited to close this financing for David Martin and the Terra team. They are one of the highest-quality sponsors in the market, and this is a Class A+ asset that is newly completed and already more than 90% leased.”
Kyle Asher, Partner And Co-Head Of Monroe Capital’s Alternative Credit Solutions Group
“The strong leasing momentum and differentiated wellness-focused concept at THE WELL Bay Harbor Islands created an opportunity to structure a refinancing that aligned with Terra’s long-term objectives.”
Keith Kurland, Senior Managing Director Of Capital Markets And Co-Head Of Institutional Advisory At Walker & Dunlop

articles.title: USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
articles.snippet:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture has announced a $180 million investment to launch its Seed Sovereignty Initiative, a program focused on protecting and better utilizing the plant genetic resources that support American agriculture.
The post USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
USDA Launches $180 Million Seed Sovereignty Initiative To Strengthen U.S. Agricultural Security
The U.S. Department of Agriculture has announced a $180 million investment to launch its Seed Sovereignty Initiative, a program focused on protecting and better utilizing the plant genetic resources that support American agriculture.
The initiative will direct new funding to the USDA Agricultural Research Service’s National Plant Germplasm System, which maintains more than 600,000 accessions representing over 16,000 species.
USDA plans to use the funding to sequence collections of major crops, identify gaps in the country’s agricultural genetic resources, and make more of the genetic information in the system available for agricultural research and crop development.
The department said the initiative is intended to strengthen U.S. agricultural security, support the development of new crop varieties, and help researchers respond more quickly to pests, diseases, and other challenges affecting agricultural production.
The effort comes as USDA seeks to better understand the genetic resources already held in U.S. collections. The department said many of these collections have not yet been fully sequenced, limiting researchers’ ability to systematically identify potentially valuable traits.
Over the next two years, USDA plans to characterize and sequence numerous collections maintained by the National Plant Germplasm System.
The department will also use advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to analyze the resulting information and identify genetic traits that could potentially benefit American agriculture.
The work could help researchers identify plant characteristics associated with areas such as resistance to emerging pests and diseases and provide additional information for the development of new crop varieties.
USDA described the National Plant Germplasm System as an important repository of agricultural genetic diversity. By combining preservation with large-scale sequencing and analysis, the department aims to make the resource more useful for researchers and agricultural producers.
The Seed Sovereignty Initiative is designed to shift USDA’s approach from primarily preserving agricultural genetic resources toward more actively understanding and strategically using them.
USDA also framed the initiative as an agricultural security measure intended to reduce potential dependence on foreign sources for important plant genetic resources and related information.
The department said foreign competitors have been acquiring and sequencing plant genetic resources from around the world while the United States has yet to fully capitalize on the genetic information within its own collections.
Alongside the $180 million initiative, USDA is expanding an existing Memorandum of Understanding with the U.S. Department of Justice related to competition in agricultural input markets.
Seeds will remain a major focus of the expanded partnership.
USDA said the effort with the Justice Department is intended to promote greater transparency, competition and choice for farmers purchasing seeds and other agricultural inputs.

articles.snippet:
Helion, an Everett, Washington-based fusion energy company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $175 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. Together with an additional $50 million in private investment, the initiative would support approximately $225 million in research and development focused on advanced semiconductor technologies needed for commercial fusion energy.
The post Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Helion Signs LOI For Up To $175 Million In CHIPS Act Funding, Supporting $225 Million Semiconductor Investment
Helion, an Everett, Washington-based fusion energy company, has signed a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $175 million in proposed funding under the CHIPS and Science Act. Together with an additional $50 million in private investment, the initiative would support approximately $225 million in research and development focused on advanced semiconductor technologies needed for commercial fusion energy.
The proposed federal funding would be administered through the Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office and support domestic research, semiconductor manufacturing, advanced packaging, and specialized equipment development.
Helion is developing fusion energy systems that use high-power electrical pulses to generate and recover energy. These systems require specialized power semiconductors capable of rapidly switching substantial amounts of electricity while maintaining efficiency, reliability, and long operating lifetimes.
According to Helion, semiconductor devices meeting its technical requirements are currently available only from overseas manufacturers. Developing domestic production capabilities would help the company reduce supply chain dependencies while supporting the commercialization of its fusion technology.
The proposed funding will support research into next-generation high-voltage semiconductors designed to deliver improved electrical efficiency, longer operating lifetimes, and more effective cooling.
More than $100 million of the investment will support semiconductor and advanced packaging research and development in Everett, Washington.
The work is expected to establish substantial power module manufacturing capabilities in the state and support the creation of more than 100 jobs.
A central component of the project involves developing advanced semiconductor packaging techniques that integrate multiple devices into efficient, scalable power modules.
These modules are expected to support the demanding electrical requirements of Helion’s fusion systems, which must repeatedly manage and recover substantial amounts of energy.
Approximately $80 million will support research into semiconductor tooling, design, and manufacturing processes in collaboration with an industry partner in Burlington, Vermont.
The initiative is intended to expand domestic capabilities for producing specialized semiconductor technologies that are important for commercial fusion power plants.
The remaining project resources will support additional improvements in semiconductor packaging and manufacturing automation.
Beyond fusion energy, the technologies being developed could have applications in electrical grid transmission, defense systems, and other industries requiring efficient management of high-power electrical systems.
The proposed federal award follows several developments in Helion’s fusion energy program during 2026.
The company previously secured $500 million in Series G funding and reported becoming the first private fusion energy company to demonstrate deuterium-tritium fusion while achieving plasma temperatures of 150 million degrees Celsius.
